newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Little, Bunce expected to miss Canberra.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Little, Bunce expected to miss Canberra.

text.p: HAMILTON, May 5 - The Waikato Chiefs' All Black midfield pairing of Walter Little and Frank Bunce seem certain to miss this week's Super 12 rugby trip to Canberra, NZPA reports.
That should leave the second five-eighths and centre berths for Friday night's game against ACT Brumbies in the hands of youngsters Scott McLeod and Pita Alatini.
Judging by the way McLeod, 24, and Alatini, 21, handled their roles in Saturday night's 47-9 whitewash of Gauteng Lions at Hamilton's Rugby Park, that should not be a problem.

Chiefs physiotherapist Dennis Shepherd said that while a decision would probably not be made until Tuesday night or Wednesday morning, both Little and Bunce were unlikely to be fit for the Australian trip.
The team fly out from Auckland early on Thursday morning after assembling in Devonport for training tomorrow.
Little has an ongoing medial ligament knee problem that Shepherd said flared up from time to time, and was hard to tell just how long it would take to come right this time.

Bunce could be out of action for a week or two, which may mean his Super 12 season has ended, as the Chiefs have only two games left. The All Black centre has a strain and partial tear of the plantar fascia tendon on the sole of his foot.
There were so many late changes to the Chiefs' line-up on Saturday night they had to slip a photocopied updated team list into the programme.
The latest withdrawal, on Saturday, was wing Eric Rush with bronchitis and the backline fielded against the Lions was different in all but two positions from the previous match.
Fullback Matthew Cooper had also been in doubt with food poisoning but recovered in time to contribute 22 points which carried him past the century mark for the season.

Shepherd is hoping Rush, fellow wing Glen Osborne (knee and calf), halfback Mark Robinson (ankle), No 8 Errol Brain (ankle), flanker Dean Anglesey (neck and thoracic spine) and lock/loose forward Blair Larsen, who were all ruled unfit for the Lions match, will be able to go to Canberra. "We've had huge problems all season," Shepherd said.
Much of it was from wear and tear due to the greater pace of the game; the lack of a decent break from last season, and training on hard grounds, he said.
"The other teams have all got the same problems. Even the South African and Australian physios and doctors I've talked to say the same thing."
